# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.

# Repository Overview: `/app` — Transaction Categorization / Enrichment Service

## 1. Overall Structure

```
/app
├── .gitignore
├── Dockerfile                          # python:3.9.2, gunicorn on port 9898, `pip3 install -e .`
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # Flask 1.1.2, pandas 1.2.4, fuzzywuzzy, python-Levenshtein, scipy, sklearn
    └── categorizationapp/              # the actual Python package
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app factory + request timing hooks (lines 7-31)
        ├── Controller.py               # HTTP endpoints; orchestrates the whole pipeline (936 lines)
        ├── BankScripts/                # 35 per-bank categorizers (SBI, HDFC, ICICI, Axis, Kotak, ...)
        └── UtilityScripts/             # shared enrichment stages + regex constants + enums
```

- It is a **Flask microservice** (single git commit `047782b "import codebase"`, branch `main`). The Docker image name reveals the project identity: `transaction-enrichment-python` (`/app/Dockerfile:3`).
- Two endpoints in `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`:
  - `POST /categorizeTransaction` (line 69, function `categorizeTransaction()`) — the main enrichment endpoint. Payload: `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `isPFMEnabled`, `transactions[]`.
  - `POST /recurrentTransactions` (line 55, `recurrentTransactions()`) — clusters transactions by party name.
- `Controller.py` is a giant if/elif over ~35 bank codes (`"SBI"` line 115, `"ICICI"` line 139, `"HDFC"` line 163, ..., `"TAMILNAD_MERCANTILE"` line 907; unknown bank returns error at line 931-932). Each branch runs the identical stage sequence.

## 2. The Enrichment Pipeline (categorization + counterparty extraction)

Per-bank flow (e.g. HDFC branch, Controller.py:163-186):

1. **`AppUtil.clean_input_df(transactions)`** — `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py:6` — normalizes description/amount/balance dtypes.
2. **`categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)`** — bank-specific file in `BankScripts/`. Assigns `transactionCategory` (default `"TRANSFER"`), initial `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, and extracts `partyName` / `party2` (counterparty).
3. **(credit cards only)** `card_clean_names()` — `UtilityScripts/CardCleanNames.py:9` and `card_purpose()` — `UtilityScripts/CardPurpose.py:9`.
4. **`purpose(transactions, accountType)`** — `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py:9` — bank-agnostic second-level categorization (subcategory + merchantType).
5. **`clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)`** — `UtilityScripts/CleanName.py:9` (1971 lines) — canonicalizes counterparty names to clean merchant names.
6. **`internal_payment(transactions, accountHolder, bank, accountType)`** — `UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py:8` — fuzzy match (`fuzzywuzzy`, threshold 75, lines 22/39) of `partyName` vs. account-holder to flag self-transfers; sets `isInternalPayment` (lines 55-60).
7. **(SAVING only)** `salary_detection(transactions)` — `UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py:16` — hierarchical clustering (Levenshtein `pdist` + `cut_tree(linkage(...), height=1.5)`, lines 25-34) plus amount-mode/frequency heuristics to label `SALARY` / `REIMBURSEMENT`.
8. **(isPFMEnabled)** `pfm_categorization()` — `UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py:8` — maps to PFM buckets; and `simple_description()` — `UtilityScripts/SimpleDescription.py:6` — builds `pfmSimpleDescription` from `partyName` + enum display names.

**Mechanism used everywhere:** lists of `[boolean-Series condition, choice]` pairs evaluated with `np.select(df['conditions'], df['choices'], default=...)` — an ordered rule cascade of pandas `str.contains(regex)` matches combined with `type.eq("DEBIT"/"CREDIT")` and amount guards.

### Bank scripts (categorization + name extraction), `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/`
Each defines one function `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(...)`:
Andhra.py, AuSmallFinanceBank.py, Axis.py, BOB.py, BOI.py, Bandhan.py, BankOfMaharashtra.py, Canara.py, Central.py, Citi.py, CityUnion.py, DCB.py, Federal.py, HDFC.py, ICICI.py, IDBI.py, IDFC.py, Indian.py, Indusind.py, Karnataka.py, KarurVyasa.py, Kotak.py, PNB.py, Paytm.py, RBL.py, SBI.py, SVC.py, Saraswat.py, SouthIndian.py, StandardCharted.py, Syndicate.py, TamilnadMerchantile.py, UCO.py, UnionBank.py, YES.py.

Representative example — **HDFC.py** (`categorize_HDFC_transactions`, line 9):
- Category rules (lines 11-101): OPENING_BALANCE (12), ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION (13), UPI/IMPS reversals (22-23), NEFT_RETURN (28), cheque rules (69-75), UPI (58), IMPS (59), NEFT (60), RTGS (61), duplicate debit/credit pair -> REVERSAL/AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE (98-99), 16-char MICR-style remark -> CHEQUE_DEPOSIT (100). Default `"TRANSFER"` (104).
- Counterparty extraction (lines 146-218): positional token splitting via `sep_by_dash/sep_by_colon/sep_by_` helpers plus `py_extract()` regex captures, e.g. `NEFT [CD][Rr]-...` field 2-3 (line 159), UPI field 1-2 (line 154), cheque patterns HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1-10 (lines 188-197), fund-transfer patterns (200-213). Cleanup and title-casing at 223, 239-247, and merchant fixups (Netflix/Amazon Prime, 268-269). `party2` = whitespace-stripped partyName (line 275).

**SBI.py** (`categorize_SBI_transactions`, line 8): ACC_VERIF penny-drop credit of Rs.1 (line 12), UPI (50), IMPS (54), NEFT (55), RTGS (56), cheque via `\bCLG\b|\bCHQ\b|CHEQUE` (45-47), NEFT/IMPS/INB name extraction with `SBI_INB_*`, `SBI_IMPS_*`, `SBI_CP_PATTERN*`, `SBI_AUTOPAY*` constants (lines 97-190).

### Shared regex constant modules
- **`UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py`** (432 lines) — per-bank narration patterns:
  - Cheque/MICR: `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1..10` (lines 81-90, e.g. `"MICR 1 CLG - NO :|- - MICR CLG -..."`, `"CHQ DEP - MICR [0-9] CLEARING..."`), `CHQ_PATTERN1..4` "MICR INWARD..." (314-317), `PNB_CHQ_0..8` (140-148), `CHQ_CLEAN_KOTAK` (318), `CHQ_CLEAN`/`CHQ_CLEAN2` (361-362), `CHQ_PENAL_KV`/`CHQ_RTN_KV` (341-342), `CHQ_RTN_PENAL_CITY` (353).
  - Fund-transfer counterparty capture: `FT_PATTERN2` (243), `FT_CHQ_PATTERN1..37` (263-299), e.g. `"^TRF FROM CHQ [0-9]+ (.*)@"`.
  - Account verification / penny drop: `ACC_VERIF` (6, contains `pennyd`), `BANK_VER_ICICI` (69, `PennyD rop|pennydrop|ny\s?drop|TestVPA|/BAV-|/BV[0-9]`), `BANK_VER_HD` (75), `BANK_VER_BOI` (110, `/PENNY D`), `ACC_VERI_UNION` (116), `ACC_VERIFY_PNB` (133), `ACC_VERI_SYNDICATE` (163), `BANK_VERIF` (321), `BANK_VER` (327), `ACC_VERI_ANDHRA` (365), `ACC_VERI_YES` (396), `ACC_VERI_RBL` (410), `ACC_VERI_CB` (415), `ACC_VERIF_PAYTM` (428), `ACC_VERI_SCB` (431).
  - `NEFT_PAYMENT_STOP` (333) — IFSC-prefix stoplist for NEFT names.
- **`UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py`** (191 lines) — bank-agnostic merchant/purpose lexicons: `LOAN_REP` (9), `LOAN` (13), `BANK_LOAN_CHQ` (18, e.g. `"KOTAK.*BANK.*LOAN|..."`), `IT_SER` (30), `MICRO_FIN` (113), plus SALARY, INSURANCE, INVEST, TRAVEL, UTILITY etc. used by Purpose.py.
- **Enums:** `UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` (class `TransactionCategory`, 171 lines; e.g. `NEFT` line 55, `IMPS` 56, `UPI` 71, `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION="Account Verification"` line 83, `CHEQUE_PAID` 27, `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` 57) and `UtilityScripts/TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` (class `TransactionSubcategory`, 135 lines). Used only by `SimpleDescription.py` for display names.

### Key rule areas you asked about

**Cheque debits / MICR:**
- HDFC.py:69-75, 100 (CHEQUE_PAID / CHEQUE_DEPOSIT / CHEQUE_RETURN; MICR-remark rule at 100); name extraction from MICR clearing narrations at 188-197.
- SBI.py:44-47 (`CHEQUE_CASH_WITHDRAWAL`, `CHEQUE_PAID`, `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` via `\bCLG\b|\bCHQ\b|CHEQUE`).
- BankRegexConstants.py: all `*_CHQ_*` and `MICR` constants listed above; Kotak MICR-inward `CHQ_PATTERN1..4` (314-317).
- CleanName.py:1745 — `"^EMI [0-9]+ CHQ"` -> "HDFC Bank Loan <num>"; HDFC.py:260 blanks partyName matching "Micr Clg|Chq Paid".
- RegexConstants.py:18 `BANK_LOAN_CHQ`, used in Purpose.py:42-43 (loan repayment/disbursal by cheque) and Purpose.py:200 (merchantType "Bank Loan").

**Transfers:** default category `"TRANSFER"` in every bank script (`np.select(..., default="TRANSFER")`, e.g. HDFC.py:104, SBI.py:70); TPT (HDFC.py:57), FUND_TRANSFER (HDFC.py:96), internet banking (SBI.py:57); `FT_*`/`FT_CHQ_*` extraction patterns (BankRegexConstants.py:243-299).

**NEFT / IMPS / UPI (credits and debits):** every bank script has an ordered trio of rules, e.g. HDFC.py:58-60, SBI.py:50/54-56, ICICI.py:61-64, Axis.py:46-49, Canara.py:57-59, Federal.py:32-34, BOB.py:55-57, etc. Charges/returns/reversals: HDFC.py:22-23 (UPI_REVERSAL/IMPS_REVERSAL), 28-29 (NEFT_RETURN/RTGS_RETURN), 34 (IMPS_CHARGES); SBI.py:17-20.

**Account-verification / penny-drop deposits:** in nearly every bank script, gated on amount ~ Rs.1:
- SBI.py:12 (`ACC_VERIF` + CREDIT + `amount.eq(1)`), HDFC.py:13 (`BANK_VER` + `amount.lt(2)`), ICICI.py:11 (`BANK_VER_ICICI` + `amount.isin([1,-1])`), Axis.py:24-26 (any Rs.1 CREDIT), Indusind.py:29-31, Kotak.py:13-14, Paytm.py:15-16 (any Rs.1 IMPS credit), BankOfMaharashtra.py:36-37, BOI.py:12, BOB.py:12, IDBI.py:12, IDFC.py:12, Karnataka.py:12, PNB.py:12, Canara.py:19, Central.py:12, UnionBank.py:12, Syndicate.py:12, Andhra.py:12, RBL.py:15, YES.py:14, StandardCharted.py:13, SouthIndian.py:12, AuSmallFinanceBank.py:12, TamilnadMerchantile.py:13.
- Purpose.py:165 — LOAN subcategory with amount 1/-1 reclassified to `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`; Purpose.py:173 blanks subcategory for VERIFICATION; SalaryDetection.py:205-206 excludes ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION/Rs.1 txns from salary.
- "penny" strings live in the regex constants: `pennyd` (BankRegexConstants.py:6), `PennyD rop|pennydrop|ny\s?drop` (69, 75, 327), `/PENNY D` (110).

**Counterparty-name extraction:** primary extraction is inside each bank script (partyName sections, e.g. HDFC.py:146-275, SBI.py:97-192) using `AppUtil.py` helpers `sep_by_` / `sep_by_dash` / `sep_by_wave` / `sep_by_star` / `sep_by_colon` etc. (AppUtil.py:14-45) and `py_extract()` (AppUtil.py:61-66). Canonicalization to clean merchant names happens in `CleanName.py:clean_names` (1971 lines of `[regex-match, "Clean Name"]` rows, e.g. lines 13-120 for DTH/broadband/electricity boards, 769 "Muthoot Microfin", 1785 "Suryoday Small Finance Bank") and `CardCleanNames.py:card_clean_names` (927 lines, e.g. line 379 "MUTHOOT MICR" -> "Muthoot Microfin").

## 3. Test Fixtures / Baseline Corpus / How Tests Are Run

**There are none in this repository.** Verified:
- No `test*/`, `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, `tox.ini`, `Makefile`, `README`, or CI config anywhere (glob for `**/{test,tests,conftest,pytest,tox,Makefile,README}*` returned nothing; `git ls-files` — 54 files total — has no match for test/fixture/baseline/corpus).
- `setup.py` declares no test framework or `tests_require`.
- The only test-related residue: `.gitignore:30` ignores `TEST*.xml` (unit test reports) and `.gitignore:52` ignores `*.csv` — suggesting a CSV-based baseline corpus and test reports existed upstream but were never committed here. Commented "For testing purpose only" dendrogram-plot blocks exist in `SalaryDetection.py:27-32` and `RecurrentTxns.py:16-21`.
- The only way to exercise the code as shipped is running the service (Dockerfile: `pip3 install -e .` then `gunicorn ... categorizationapp:app` on port 9898, or `python -m categorizationapp` via `__init__.py:30-31`) and POSTing JSON to `/categorizeTransaction`.

## 4. Pipeline Flow Summary

```
POST /categorizeTransaction (Controller.py:69)
  -> AppUtil.clean_input_df                       (AppUtil.py:6)
  -> categorize_<BANK>_transactions               (BankScripts/<Bank>.py)
       ordered np.select regex cascade over `description` + type/amount guards
       sets: transactionCategory (default TRANSFER), partyName, party2
       rules: ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION (Rs.1 penny-drop), CHQ/MICR cheque paid/deposit/return,
              NEFT/IMPS/UPI/RTGS, ATM, charges, reversals, auto-pay/NACH, FD/RD ...
  -> [CREDIT_CARD] card_clean_names / card_purpose (CardCleanNames.py:9 / CardPurpose.py:9)
  -> purpose(transactions, accountType)            (Purpose.py:9)
       transactionSubcategory (SALARY, LOAN, LOAN_REPAYMENT, INSURANCE, RENT, ...)
       + category overrides (e.g. LOAN @ Rs.1 -> ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION, line 165)
       + merchantType (NBFC, Bank Loan, Micro Finance Institution, Streaming, ...)
  -> clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)  (CleanName.py:9)   # canonical merchant names
  -> internal_payment(...)                         (InternalPayment.py:8)  # fuzzy self-transfer detection
  -> [SAVING] salary_detection(...)                (SalaryDetection.py:16) # Levenshtein clustering + mode heuristics
  -> [PFM] pfm_categorization / simple_description (PFMCategorization.py:8 / SimpleDescription.py:6)
  -> JSON response (Controller.py:934-936)
```

Everything is deterministic regex/rule based (no ML models at inference other than the Levenshtein clustering for salary/recurrence grouping); rule order matters because `np.select` takes the first matching condition.

def run(fn, rows):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["description", "type", "amount", "balanceAfterTransaction", "remark"])
    df["remark"] = df["remark"].astype(str)
    out = fn(df.copy(), "SAVING")
    return out[["description", "type", "amount", "transactionCategory", "partyName"]]

from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.Purpose import purpose
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.CleanName import clean_names
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.InternalPayment import internal_payment


def full_pipeline(rows, accountType="SAVING"):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["description", "type", "amount", "balanceAfterTransaction", "remark"])
    df["remark"] = df["remark"].astype(str)
    out = categorize_AuSmallFinance_transactions(df.copy(), accountType)
    out = purpose(out, accountType)
    out = clean_names(out, accountType, "AU_SMALL_FINANCE_BANK")
    out = internal_payment(out, "Account Holder Name", "AU_SMALL_FINANCE_BANK", accountType)
    return out[["description", "type", "amount", "transactionCategory", "transactionSubcategory", "partyName"]]

steps.message:
All five findings traced to a single script — `categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/AuSmallFinanceBank.py` — and fixed there. I confirmed the bank empirically: replaying each finding's narration shape through every candidate categorizer, only the AU Small Finance script reproduces all five symptoms exactly (notably F-4's "bare reference number *surfaces*" — Canara/HDFC would have blanked a numeric name in their cleanup passes, so the finding could only come from this script).

## Root causes and fixes

| Finding | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **F-1** bare-number cheque debit → TRANSFER | Cheque rule (line 38) only matches textual notes (`BY CLG`/`Chq Paid`); a note that is just the 6-digit instrument number matches nothing and falls to the `TRANSFER` default | New rule: `^[0-9]{6}$` + DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID` (AuSmallFinanceBank.py:39) |
| **F-2** `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` → name = "Micr Clg" | Generic `^CHQ PAID-` extraction takes dash-token 1, which in this layout is the `MICR CLG` clearing tag, not the name | Specific rule ahead of it: `^CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-` → token 2 (AuSmallFinanceBank.py:81) |
| **F-3** plain NEFT credits → blank name | Only the `NEFT CR-` (space) layout is extracted; the dashed `NEFT-CR-…-NAME` variant matches no extraction rule at all | New rule: `^NEFT-[CD][Rr]-` → token 3 (AuSmallFinanceBank.py:66) |
| **F-4** IMPS P2P credit → name = bare reference | Generic `IMPS-` rule takes token 2, correct for `IMPS-<ref>-<name>` but for `IMPS-CR-<ref>-<name>` token 2 is the RRN, which surfaces verbatim | Guarded rule ahead of it: `^IMPS-[CD][Rr]-[0-9]+-` → token 3; the `[0-9]+-` guard means it can only fire where the old rule produced a number, so name-at-token-2 layouts are untouched (AuSmallFinanceBank.py:58) |
| **F-5** ₹1 confirmation credit → TRANSFER | Verification rule covers `Acc validation`, `AC VALIDATION`, and OCR-split `A/ C VALIDATION` — but not the standard `A/C VALIDATION` form (the slash breaks the `AC` match) | Added `A/C VALIDATION` alternative to the rule (AuSmallFinanceBank.py:12) |

## Verification (deterministic, offline — matching QA's replay method)

- Each finding's narration form now derives the baseline field through the **full enrichment chain** (bank categorizer → `purpose` → `clean_names` → `internal_payment`): `CHEQUE_PAID`, "Ravi Kumar", "John Doe", "Ravi Kumar", `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`.
- **No-regression sweep**: ran 34 ordinary narrations (UPI/IMPS/NEFT/RTGS variants, other cheque layouts, charges, ATM, deposits, refunds, salary, long numeric refs, bare-number *credits*, non-₹1 `A/C VALIDATION`) through the git-HEAD version vs. the fixed version — **0 differences**. Every fix is gated so it can only fire on rows that previously produced the regressed (wrong or blank) value.

Note: the repo contains no committed fixture corpus or test suite (`.gitignore` excludes `*.csv`/`TEST*.xml`), so verification was done with a standalone harness in `/tmp/opencode`; nothing outside the one bank script was modified.
